blocks.value: Java provides the `String` class from the `java.lang` package to create and manipulate strings. It has its own methods for working with text. **The `String` class is not a primitive data type.**

A **string is a sequence of characters**. Every character has a specific position, and the position of the first character starts at **index 0**. The **length** of a string is the number of characters in it.
Note what that means: the **last valid index is always `length() - 1`**, here `10`. Asking for index 11 throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. The space at index 5 is a character like any other.

An **empty string** `""` is a real string with no characters, so its length is `0` and you can call methods on it. A `null` string is no string at all: the variable points to nothing, and calling any method on it throws `NullPointerException`:
